title: Input and Output
summary: Programs talk to users through input and output. Output prints messages; input reads what the user types.
learningObjectives: Apply the concept in a small program
Predict program output by reading code

sections.content: Programs talk to users through input and output. Output prints messages; input reads what the user types.
Every language has a standard way to print. Input is a bit more varied — some languages read from the console, others from files or the network.
Key points: printing is your main debugging tool early on, and always check what type input arrives as — it often starts as text.

sections.codeExample:
echo "Alice";
// The line above sends text to the screen

sections.content: Summary: Input and Output — practice the example by changing values and predicting the output before running it.

keyTakeaways: Key points: printing is your main debugging tool early on, and always check what type input arrives as — it often starts as text.
